description: Stateful Robotics is an embodied AI company developing decision intelligence technology for mobile robots operating in unpredictable, real-world environments. Its platform builds a persistent model of tasks, environments and past behaviour, enabling robots to plan over longer time horizons, adapt to disruption, and perform more reliably in the field. Already live with pilot customers in sectors such as infrastructure and logistics, Stateful is bringing an essential intelligence layer to robotics deployments where tightly scripted approaches break down. Spun out from the University of Oxford, the company is focused on helping autonomous systems scale more effectively across complex industrial environments.
tagline: Stateful Robotics is an embodied AI company developing decision intelligence technology for mobile robots operating in unpredictable, real-world environments. Its platform helps robots plan over longer time horizons, adapt to disruption, and perform more reliably in the field.

description: OKAPI:Orbits is a German software-as-a-service start-up making space operations safer and more sustainable through collision avoidance and space traffic management. As experts in Space Situational Awareness and Space Surveillance & Tracking, the company provides continuous monitoring, conjunction prediction, and alerting services, and recommends evasive manoeuvres to protect valuable space assets and reduce debris creation. Backed by the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund.
tagline: OKAPI:Orbits delivers SaaS-based space traffic management that monitors, predicts, and mitigates collision risks—backed by the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund.

description: UniSieve enables the scalable fabrication of mechanically flexible molecular-sieving membranes that separate hydrocarbons and CO₂ via a size-exclusion mechanism—replacing energy-intensive thermal distillation. By adopting UniSieve’s separation solutions, customers cut energy use, reduce emissions, improve their carbon footprint, and increase product recovery. Backed by the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund.
tagline: UniSieve develops flexible molecular-sieve membranes that deliver low-energy hydrocarbon and CO₂ separations—improving yields and shrinking emissions—backed by the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund.

description: ATMOS Space Cargo delivers a scalable, cost-efficient solution to bring cargo back from space. Its Inflatable Atmospheric Decelerators (IADs) act first as a heat shield and then as a high-velocity parachute, protecting payloads during re-entry. The approach is tailored to each object—from shoebox-sized experiments to the largest rocket stages—enabling safe, repeatable recovery at low cost. Backed by the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund.
tagline: ATMOS Space Cargo uses inflatable atmospheric decelerators to provide safe, scalable, and cost-efficient re-entry for payloads of all sizes—backed by the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund.

description: Vertus Energy develops ground-breaking technology that uses electricity to stimulate bacteria in anaerobic digestion (AD), dramatically increasing biogas output. Its product, BRIO, enables AD plants to process 3× more waste in the same tank while delivering biogas with 60% higher energy potential. BRIO can be retrofitted to existing facilities as well as deployed in new builds, allowing seamless testing and integration without interrupting ongoing digestion processes. Backed by the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund.
tagline: Vertus Energy’s BRIO electrifies anaerobic digesters to triple throughput and boost biogas energy content by 60%, with retrofit-ready integration—backed by the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund.

description: GEMESYS is developing the architecture for a fully analogue AI chip inspired by the human brain, delivering step-change resource efficiency to overcome today’s compute bottlenecks and enable truly efficient edge AI. The design mirrors key brain-like information-processing mechanisms, allowing AI hardware vendors to offer a novel chip that supports both on-device inference and training—cutting latency and energy use while improving privacy. Backed by the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund.
tagline: GEMESYS is building brain-inspired analogue AI chips that enable low-power, low-latency on-device training and inference—backed by the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund.

description: HyperHeat develops ultra-efficient electric heaters to decarbonise heavy industry by replacing fossil fuels in high-temperature process heat, which accounts for 20% of global CO₂ emissions. Its breakthrough hot-air system reaches up to 2,000 °C with 95–98% efficiency and is designed for rapid integration, scalability, and low degradation—enabling megatonne-scale CO₂ reductions across sectors such as steel, cement, and chemicals. Backed by the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund.
tagline: HyperHeat provides 2,000 °C, 95–98% efficient electric process heaters that replace fossil fuels in heavy industry—backed by the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund.

description: enaDyne is a Leipzig-based climate tech company developing modular, fully electric, non-thermal plasma reactors that convert CO₂ and other process gases into valuable chemicals and abate hard-to-treat emissions such as CF₄ and PFAS. With a patented electrode and catalyst platform, enaDyne combines high energy efficiency, operational flexibility, and scalable, containerised deployment—enabling customers to produce sustainable chemicals at or below fossil prices. Backed by the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund, the company operates as a technology OEM with recurring revenues from proprietary consumables.
tagline: enaDyne builds containerised, fully electric plasma-catalysis reactors that upcycle CO₂ into chemicals with high efficiency—backed by the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund.

description: Periphery (formerly Qomodo) is a UK-based cybersecurity company securing the edge of critical systems—from drones and autonomous vehicles to industrial sensors and battlefield technologies. Designed for the embedded and extended Internet of Things (XIoT), Periphery’s platform defends the world’s most resource-constrained and security-critical devices against modern threats. Founded by former NATO and BAE Systems engineers, Periphery provides lightweight, AI-driven software agents that embed directly onto devices—enabling real-time threat detection, anomaly monitoring, and lifecycle protection without compromising performance. Its zero-trust architecture and in-device observability ensure compliance with global cybersecurity standards, including the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), NIS2, and IEC 62443. Periphery’s solutions are deployed globally, including in active conflict zones, where its technology helps protect drone fleets and autonomous systems in hostile environments.
tagline: Periphery is a UK-based cybersecurity company protecting resource-constrained XIoT devices with AI-powered, in-device threat detection and compliance-ready lifecycle security.

description: Recurvia (previously known as Inephany) is a London-based deep-tech start-up, founded in July 2024, that pioneers foundation models designed to automate and optimise how other AI systems are trained, tuned and deployed. Its real-time, AI-driven optimisation platform intelligently controls the training process, boosting sample efficiency, accelerating convergence and raising final model performance while slashing compute costs and energy use — an order-of-magnitude leap over traditional trial-and-error methods. The company was founded by Dr John Torr (ex-Apple Siri) and Maurice von Sturm (co-founders of conversational-AI start-up Wluper) and is chaired by AI pioneer Professor Steve Young. Together this team of engineers, research scientists and entrepreneurs is rethinking AI at a system level to make cutting-edge models faster, greener and more affordable across domains ranging from large language models to computer vision and time-series forecasting.
tagline: Recurvia optimises foundational AI models to cut the cost, time and energy required to train and deploy state-of-the-art AI systems.

description: Ciphergen Biosystems developed a unique technology, using a patented protein chip to detect proteins within biological samples. The technology proved efficient and cost-effective. Ciphergen customers included many of the largest pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies worldwide, as well as government agencies, research institutions and universities. Working with customers to develop new products and applications, Ciphergen became a leader in biomarker discovery, assay development and characterisation. Amadeus invested in Ciphergen in its $29 million pre-IPO financing round in March 2000. The company successfully floated on NASDAQ.
tagline: Ciphergen Biosystems developed a patented protein chip to detect proteins within biological samples. The company successfully floated on NASDAQ.-

description: Oxford Nanopore Technologies, founded in 2005, developed a novel generation of DNA/RNA sequencing technology that delivers rich data, is fast, accessible, and easy to use. The company aims to disrupt conventional biological analysis and enable new applications with a profound, positive impact on society. Its sequencing technology is used across a wide range of biological research areas—including human genetics, cancer, agriculture, food science, environmental monitoring, and pathogen analysis. Oxford Nanopore’s platform has been deployed in over 70 countries to sequence SARS-CoV-2, the virus responsible for COVID-19.
tagline: Oxford Nanopore Technologies develops scalable, real-time DNA/RNA sequencing tools that enable fast, accessible analysis across research, healthcare, and global diagnostics.

description: V7 is building the foundation for Trustworthy AI—unleashing the true power of artificial intelligence by combining machine efficiency with human insight. The company draws inspiration from the human visual cortex—specifically the six areas, V1 through V6, that enable the brain to interpret shape, colour, motion, and meaning. Just as the Cambrian explosion 540 million years ago gave rise to the sense of sight and an explosion of diversity, V7 aims to spark a new era of “living software”—granting machines the power of vision and multiplying the tasks they can perform.
tagline: V7 builds Trustworthy AI systems that combine human insight with foundation models to deliver scalable, vision-powered automation across critical industries.

description: Altana AI is a US-based technology company on a mission to improve global commerce through AI-powered value chain intelligence. Founded by leaders in supply chain artificial intelligence, the company helps governments, enterprises, and financial institutions build safe, lawful, inclusive, and resilient supply chains. Altana’s platform—the world’s first value chain management system—provides deep visibility and real-time risk intelligence across global supply networks, without requiring users to share sensitive data. By mapping and understanding complex, dynamic trade relationships, Altana enables smarter decision-making at the speed of commerce. The company works with customs authorities and multinational enterprises across North America, Europe, and Asia to drive more secure, compliant, and transparent global trade.
tagline: Altana AI created the world’s first value chain management system to help governments and enterprises build safer, more transparent, and resilient global supply networks.

description: Founded in 2016, Pimloc builds deep learning systems to protect and manage sensitive visual data in video and image collections. Its proprietary AI platform, Secure Redact, enables private and public organisations to automate video redaction, protect personal data by default, and meet data privacy compliance—280x faster than manual processes. Trained on real-world, low-quality footage from sources like CCTV, body cams, and smartphones, Secure Redact can intelligently remove faces, number plates, or other identifiers. Pimloc’s technology is trusted across mobility, insurance, broadcasting, law enforcement, and more—unlocking the value of video while ensuring privacy is preserved.
tagline: Pimloc is an AI company specialising in video redaction and visual data privacy, helping organisations automate compliance while safely unlocking the value of real-world footage.

description: Quibim is a leader in imaging biomarkers for life sciences, pioneering advanced algorithms that transform medical imaging data into actionable predictions in oncology, immunology, and neurology. Headquartered in Valencia, the company employs more than 90 people and has built a diverse team of AI specialists from over 10 nationalities. Quibim has also expanded globally, with offices in Madrid, Barcelona, New York, and Cambridge (UK).
tagline: Quibim is a medtech company turning imaging data into predictive insights to drive precision medicine in oncology, neurology, and immunology.

description: Xampla has created the world’s first plant protein material for commercial use. A spin-out from the University of Cambridge, Xampla’s mission is to replace everyday single-use plastics, like bags, sachets and flexible packing film, and microplastics within liquids and lotions. Existing natural, primarily polysaccharide materials typically cannot match the performance of plastic without chemical additions. Xampla’s plant protein material does not require linking with harmful solvents to make it a viable alternative to synthetic polymers.
tagline: Xampla is a Cambridge-based materials science company pioneering plant protein-based alternatives to single-use plastics.

description: XYZ Reality is a construction technology company revolutionising the industry with the XYZ Atom™, the world’s first Engineering Grade Augmented Reality (AR) headset. XYZ Atom™ allows construction teams to build directly from holograms instead of traditional 2D plans—positioning design models on site with up to 5mm accuracy. By enabling real-time, on-site decision-making, the technology significantly reduces errors ‘out of tolerance’ and shortens the timeline from set-out to build—addressing the root causes of delay in 77% of large-scale projects globally. XYZ Reality is also focused on making the lives of construction workers easier by democratising the skill-set, boosting productivity and closing a skills-gap
tagline: XYZ Reality is a construction tech company combining engineering-grade AR with a real-time delivery platform, giving teams full project visibility and the tools to build faster, safer, and with unmatched precision.

description: Ori Biotech is on a mission to enable widespread patient access to life-saving cell and gene therapies. As a first step towards achieving this mission, the company launched IRO®—a next-generation CGT manufacturing platform designed to automate better biology and accelerate therapy development. The platform helps make advanced therapies more affordable and accessible to patients worldwide.
tagline: Ori Biotech is a cell and gene therapy manufacturing company whose IRO® platform automates and accelerates production to make advanced therapies more scalable, affordable, and accessible.

description: Nu Quantum is building the quantum networking infrastructure essential to scaling quantum computers. To deliver transformational impact, quantum computers must scale from hundreds to hundreds of thousands of qubits. Nu Quantum’s approach interconnects many smaller cores using a Quantum Networking Unit (QNU), enabling the efficient scaling of discrete Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) into larger, more powerful quantum systems. The company is developing full hardware solutions to create entangled qubit networks—including a proprietary high-speed network interface, photonic switching fabric, and advanced control systems—laying the foundation for multi-core quantum supercomputers and quantum data centres. In partnership with leading quantum companies, governments, and research groups, Nu Quantum is accelerating the transition of quantum technology from the lab to real-world deployment. Founded in 2018, the company is a spin-out from the University of Cambridge’s Cavendish Laboratory.
tagline: Nu Quantum is a Cambridge spin-out developing quantum networking hardware to interconnect QPUs, enabling the scalable, multi-core quantum computers of the future.

description: Founded at Imperial College London, Sprout.ai empowers insurers to settle claims in as little as 24 hours by delivering data-driven insights. The company specialises in deep search and data enrichment to validate, investigate, and automate the context of insurance claims—a first in the industry. Sprout.ai combines AI with external data sources to streamline claims processing. By analysing vast volumes of data, it enables insurers to build objective, evidence-based narratives around incidents that are typically difficult to assess. Working with major insurance companies across three continents, Sprout.ai helps increase fraud detection rates, lower operating costs, accelerate settlement times, and maintain industrial-grade security. Sprout.ai works with major insurance companies across three continents to deliver increased fraud detection rates, reduced operating costs, faster claim settlement times and industrial grade security.
tagline: Sprout.ai uses AI and deep search technology to automate and accelerate insurance claims by generating accurate, data-rich insights in real time.

description: Riverlane’s mission is to make quantum computing useful sooner—ushering in an era of human progress as profound as the industrial and digital revolutions. To achieve this, the company is building Deltaflow, the Quantum Error Correction Stack designed to fix the millions of data errors that currently prevent quantum computers from reaching useful scale. Riverlane works with governments, quantum hardware companies, and world-leading research institutions to accelerate the commercial viability of quantum technology.
tagline: Riverlane is a quantum computing company developing Deltaflow, a Quantum Error Correction Stack that enables quantum computers to scale and deliver real-world impact sooner.

description: Entropic Inc. was a pioneering company in the field of speech recognition technology, known for its deep roots in academic research and advanced signal processing tools. Originally spun out of the Washington Research Laboratory in the mid-1980s, Entropic developed industry-leading software for speech and signal analysis, including the widely adopted ESPS/waves+ toolkit. The company played a significant role in refining Hidden Markov Model (HMM) techniques, which became foundational to modern speech recognition systems. With offices in Washington, DC and Cambridge, UK, Entropic delivered high-accuracy voice recognition engines tailored for telephony and transcription systems, offering end-to-end solutions that included software, telephony interfaces, and hardware integration. Its reputation for precision and innovation led to its acquisition by Microsoft in 1999, where its technology and expertise were used to enhance Microsoft’s speech platform and developer tools.
tagline: Entropic Inc. was a speech recognition pioneer whose signal processing software and HMM innovations laid the groundwork for modern voice systems. It was acquired by Microsoft in 1999.

description: VocalIQ was a Cambridge-based AI start-up spun out from the University of Cambridge’s Spoken Dialogue Systems Group. The company specialised in advanced voice interfaces, combining expertise in speech recognition, natural language understanding, dialogue design, and speech synthesis to create intelligent, adaptive spoken language systems. VocalIQ developed customisable voice-based interfaces for a wide range of applications—from smartphones and in-car systems to call centres, robots, and games. Its platform stood out for its ability to learn from real-world conversations, improving accuracy and context awareness over time—making interactions feel more natural and less scripted than conventional voice assistants. The company’s technology attracted significant interest in the fast-growing voice AI space, and in September 2015, VocalIQ was acquired by Apple. The acquisition was seen as a strategic move to enhance Apple’s voice capabilities, contributing to the advancement of Siri and laying foundations for more human-like conversational AI.
tagline: VocalIQ was a Cambridge-based voice AI start-up developing adaptive, learning-based spoken language systems. It was acquired in 2015 by Apple to strengthen its conversational interface technology.

description: Transmode was a provider of optical networking solutions for transporting data, voice, and video traffic, using CWDM and DWDM technologies (Coarse and Dense Wavelength Division Multiplexing). Its comprehensive product portfolio and global presence enabled customers to cost-effectively expand capacity and enhance service quality across regional, metro, and metro-access networks—without compromising on performance. The company went public on Stockholm’s NASDAQ OMX exchange in May 2011 and was acquired by US-based Infinera in August 2015.
tagline: Transmode delivered optical networking solutions using CWDM and DWDM technologies to help telecom operators expand network capacity and performance efficiently. It listed on Stockholm NASDAQ OMX in 2011 and was acquired by Infinera in 2015.

description: Optos was a medical technology company that developed a patient-friendly instrument capable of capturing a digital image of nearly the entire retina, known as an ‘Optomap’. This technology enabled optometrists to screen for a range of conditions—including diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and age-related macular degeneration—which can be effectively treated if detected early. The company was listed on the London Stock Exchange in February 2006 and was acquired by Nikon for $400m in 2015.
tagline: Optos was a medtech company whose Optomap imaging technology enabled early detection of retinal diseases through non-invasive, wide-field digital scans. It listed on the London Stock Exchange in 2006 and was acquired by Nikon for $400m in 2015.

description: Solexa developed systems for the comprehensive and cost-effective analysis of individual genomes, with the goal of transforming biological and medical research through rapid, affordable sequencing—a foundational capability for 21st-century science. The company aimed to reduce the cost of human resequencing to just a few thousand dollars, ultimately achieving the ‘$1,000 genome’ for widespread use in research and clinical diagnostics. Solexa was acquired by Illumina in January 2007. Amadeus sold its final holdings in Illumina in July 2008.
tagline: Solexa developed next-generation genome sequencing technology to make high-speed, low-cost DNA analysis accessible for research and clinical diagnostics. It was acquired by Illumina in 2007.

description: Icera was a fabless semiconductor company specialising in high-performance wireless modem technology for next-generation mobile devices. Renowned for its innovative baseband processor and advanced multimode modem solutions, the company enabled handset and device manufacturers to deliver differentiated, low-power, and cost-effective cellular products with enhanced speed and flexibility. By pioneering software-defined modem platforms, Icera offered a unique level of adaptability in a rapidly evolving wireless market—consistently meeting and exceeding the technical demands of the world’s leading mobile manufacturers. Its technology played a pivotal role in shaping the evolution of wireless connectivity across smartphones, tablets, and other mobile broadband devices. In May 2011, Icera was acquired by NVIDIA, which integrated its modem and RF capabilities to enhance mobile computing and wireless communications.
tagline: Icera was a semiconductor innovator whose software-defined modems powered next-generation mobile devices and helped redefine wireless performance. It was acquired by NVIDIA in 2011.

description: Element 14 (E14) was an independent fabless silicon chip company that produced the industry’s highest port count broadband xDSL central office concentrator chip. At the core of its design was a high-speed, low-power computing engine built to meet the growing demand for broadband services. The company was acquired by Broadcom for $642 million in November 2000.
tagline: Element 14 was a fabless semiconductor company that developed chips to enable the rapid expansion of broadband connectivity. It was acquired by Broadcom for $642m in 2000.

description: One of Amadeus’ earliest and most successful investments, CSR (formerly Cambridge Silicon Radio) was a pioneering developer of single-chip wireless solutions for short-range data and voice communications. Its technology, based on the 2.4GHz Bluetooth standard, enabled mass-market adoption through highly integrated ICs with embedded software—bringing wireless connectivity to mobile phones, digital cameras, MP3 players, and other compact consumer devices. CSR completed its IPO in February 2004. Amadeus sold its final stock holding in the open market and exited the company in 2005. CSR was later acquired by Qualcomm in August 2015.
tagline: CSR was a Bluetooth semiconductor pioneer whose single-chip wireless solutions brought short-range connectivity to the mass market and powered the rise of mobile consumer devices.

description: Bellco, an Italian company with more than 40 years’ experience, was one of the pioneers in the history of haemodialysis. Bellco operated worldwide, offering systems for the treatment of renal failure, multiple organ failure, sepsis and cardiac decompensation. Its mission was to satisfy the needs of patients and experts through innovation, research and the development of advanced and personalized therapies for nephrology, intensive care and cardiology patients. Bellco was acquired by Medtronic in February 2016.
tagline: Bellco was a pioneer in haemodialysis, they were acquired by Medtronic in 2016.

description: AePONA provided the software engine that powers the “Network as a Service” (NaaS) business model for mobile operators. With AePONA’s solution, a mobile operator can monetise important assets and functionality within its network. These include billing, location, messaging and voice communications where new revenue opportunities can be opened up. AePONA Group Ltd was acquired by Intel in April 2013.
tagline: AePONA provided the software engine that powers the “Network as a Service” (NaaS) business model for mobile operators.

description: PolyAI powers the world’s most lifelike AI voice agents for enterprises that prioritise exceptional customer experiences. Its end-to-end service automation systems handle the work of thousands—delivering fully immersive, human-like conversations with industry-leading tone and understanding. Trusted by leading global brands, PolyAI’s agents manage the majority of inbound customer service calls, eliminating wait times and allowing human staff to focus on complex or exceptional cases. This drives improved revenue, customer satisfaction, and operational efficiency.
tagline: PolyAI develops voice-first AI agents that deliver human-level customer service at scale, helping global enterprises automate support, reduce wait times, and enhance user experience.

description: XMOS is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Bristol, UK, on a mission to transform how systems are deployed on silicon. By enabling embedded software engineers to create custom system-on-chip (SoC) solutions through software alone, XMOS is disrupting SoC economics and accelerating time to market. The company offers the industry’s broadest portfolio of far-field voice-capture solutions, including both circular and linear arrays—designed to support a wide variety of consumer applications. These solutions are powered by voice-specific AI and signal processing algorithms, each individually tunable to meet precise customer requirements.
tagline: XMOS is a UK-based fabless semiconductor company enabling software-defined, customisable SoC solutions for voice and embedded applications.

description: OrganOx is a medical technology company based in Oxford, UK, that has developed metra—a groundbreaking device for preserving donor livers at normal body temperature for extended periods. The metra is commercially available within the EU and is transforming liver transplantation practices. The company was founded in 2008 to commercialise technology invented by Professor Peter Friend and further developed by Professor Constantin Coussios at the University of Oxford. Its normothermic liver perfusion device is helping redefine the standards of donor organ preservation.
tagline: OrganOx is a medtech company pioneering normothermic liver perfusion with its metra device, improving transplant outcomes and increasing the use of donor organs worldwide. It was acquired by Terumo for $1.5 billion in 2025.

description: Tobii, founded in 2001, is the global leader in remote eye tracking solutions. The company’s mission is to establish eye tracking as a core mode of Human-Machine Interaction and to integrate the technology into personal computers, tablets, and a wide range of consumer and professional applications. Headquartered in Sweden, Tobii has a global presence with offices in the United States, China, Japan, Germany, the United Kingdom, Norway, Taiwan, and South Korea, supported by a worldwide network of resellers. Tobii was listed on Nasdaq Stockholm in 2015 (STO:TOBII).
tagline: Tobii is the global leader in remote eye tracking, developing technology that powers next-generation human-machine interaction across consumer and professional applications. The company listed on Nasdaq Stockholm in 2015.

description: SLAMcore offers Spatial AI solutions for ground-based and aerial robots, enabling them to understand and navigate their environments with precision. Its algorithms convert sensor data into spatial intelligence—closing the loop between perception and action for autonomous machines. Originally a spin-out from Imperial College London, SLAMcore’s team includes world-leading experts with decades of experience delivering real-world robotics applications. The company focuses on multi-sensor, on-board solutions with particular strengths in computer vision and inertial-based approaches.
tagline: SLAMcore is a Spatial AI company providing real-time localisation and mapping software that enables robots to understand and interact with the world around them.

description: Ravelin is an award-winning fraud detection and prevention platform designed for online merchants and the payments industry. The company uses a combination of machine learning, graph networks, and expert insight to detect and block fraud before the point of sale—saving merchants millions in chargebacks, customer churn, and reputational damage.
tagline: Ravelin is a fraud prevention platform that uses machine learning and graph-based analysis to help online merchants detect and stop fraud before it happens.

description: Secondmind is the provider of the world’s first AI-powered decision-making platform. Focused on the automotive sector, Secondmind helps engineers design better cars, faster. Its cloud-native software, powered by Secondmind Active Learning, reduces simulation time and calibration overhead—streamlining development and accelerating the transition to carbon-neutral mobility. Founded in 2016, the company has been recognised with the Automotive Testing Technology International ‘Alternative Powertrain Test Innovation of the Year Award’, selected for the Tech Nation Future Fifty scale-up programme, and named by Bloomberg as one of the UK’s top 25 startups to watch. Secondmind operates from offices in Cambridge (UK) and Yokohama (Japan).
tagline: Secondmind is the provider of the world’s first AI-powered decision-making platform, helping automotive engineers design better cars, faster.

description: PhoreMost is unlocking the full potential of TPD through its proprietary target identification platforms, SITESEEKER® and GlueSEEKER®, pioneering the use of mini-protein engineering to develop novel therapeutic strategies. Targeted Protein Degradation (TPD) is a promising approach to eliminating toxic or disease-associated proteins from cells, offering a powerful strategy to address previously undruggable targets. Despite the existence of over 600 known E3 ligases, the pharmaceutical industry remains largely dependent on a limited set—such as Cereblon—for degrader-based drug development. The company has advanced several next-generation ligase programmes through proof-of-concept and is progressing multiple degrader assets toward preclinical studies. PhoreMost has also established a number of strategic partnerships, including disclosed alliances with Roche, Boehringer Ingelheim, and Sentinel Oncology.
tagline: PhoreMost is a biotech company expanding the potential of targeted protein degradation through novel mini-protein engineering and proprietary platforms to develop next-generation degrader therapies.

description: Paragraf is the first company in the world to mass-produce graphene-based electronic devices using standard semiconductor processes. Its Hall sensors and Field-Effect Transistors (FETs), currently in production, along with other semiconductor devices in development, are built on a proprietary graphene growth process that unlocks the full potential of this extraordinary 2D material. The company’s products offer exceptional sensitivity, robustness, and energy efficiency—addressing critical challenges across a wide range of sectors including automotive, industrial automation, cryogenics, healthcare, and agri-tech.
tagline: Paragraf is a graphene electronics company pioneering mass production of graphene-based devices to transform semiconductor performance across sectors from automotive to healthcare.

description: Openbravo was a global cloud Point-of-Sale (POS) and retail management software provider for agile retailing. Its flexible, cloud-based platform enabled retailers and restaurants to deliver truly unified commerce experiences, with the agility to innovate quickly and adapt to evolving shopping behaviours and business needs. In November 2022, Openbravo was acquired by French enterprise software company DL Software.
tagline: Openbravo was a cloud-based retail software company enabling agile, unified commerce experiences for retailers and restaurants worldwide. It was acquired by DL Software in 2022.

description: Natrox® is a transformative therapy brought to market by Cambridge-based Inotec AMD to accelerate healing in the most challenging wounds. Now recognised as a new global standard for treating acute and chronic wounds, Natrox® is setting a powerful benchmark: up to 90% of patients with complex wounds heal within 8–12 weeks. Patients around the world are already experiencing successful outcomes, and the company continues to secure reimbursement in key markets. Natrox® is FDA 510(k) cleared, CE (IIb) marked, and reimbursed in several regions. The patented technology—developed at the University of Cambridge—extracts moisture from ambient air and converts it into oxygen, delivering pure humidified oxygen directly to the wound bed under any dressing at a continuous flow rate.
tagline: Natrox® is an advanced wound care therapy developed in Cambridge that delivers continuous topical oxygen to accelerate healing in acute and chronic wounds.

description: Igenomix is a global leader in reproductive genetic services, advancing women’s health and fertility care through cutting-edge genetic testing and research. Founded in 2011 as a spin-out from the Instituto Valenciano de Infertilidad (IVI), the company quickly became a trusted partner to fertility clinics and healthcare professionals worldwide. It offers a comprehensive portfolio of genetic diagnostic services aimed at improving reproductive outcomes, including preimplantation genetic testing, carrier screening, and personalised fertility assessments. With a strong foundation in scientific innovation and clinical collaboration, Igenomix has played a pivotal role in increasing the success rates of assisted reproductive technologies and providing patients with deeper insight into their reproductive health. In 2019, the company was acquired by EQT, a global private equity firm, to support its continued growth and expansion across the women’s health and fertility sectors.
tagline: Igenomix is a reproductive genetics company providing advanced diagnostic testing to improve fertility outcomes and support women’s health globally. It was acquired by EQT in 2019.

description: Healx is a generative AI-enabled, clinical-stage rare disease biotech pioneering the next generation of drug discovery to bring novel, effective treatments to rare disease patients around the world. Of the 10,000 known rare diseases affecting 400 million people globally, only 5% have an approved treatment. By combining generative AI technology with deep drug discovery and development expertise, Healx accelerates the pace, increases the scale, and improves the success rate of rare disease treatment development—delivering meaningful impact for patients worldwide. The company exists because every rare disease patient deserves a treatment. Healx was founded in Cambridge, UK, by Tim Guilliams, Ph.D., a biochemical engineer and tech entrepreneur, and David Brown, Ph.D., co-inventor of Viagra and former global head of drug discovery at Roche.
tagline: Healx is a Cambridge-based biotech using generative AI to accelerate drug discovery and develop treatments for rare diseases that currently lack approved therapies.

description: Forescout Technologies helps Global 2000 enterprises and government agencies “make the invisible visible” by delivering agentless visibility, compliance and control for every IT, IoT and OT device the moment it connects to the network. Founded in 2000 and headquartered in San Jose, California, Forescout’s platform provides continuous asset discovery, network segmentation, zero-trust enforcement and automated response across campus, data-centre, cloud and industrial environments — integrating with dozens of third-party security tools to break down silos and accelerate incident response. Forescout listed on NASDAQ in 2017.
tagline: Forescout Technologies delivers agentless visibility, compliance and control for every IT, IoT and OT device on enterprise networks, underpinning zero-trust security at global scale. Listed on NASDAQ in 2017.

description: The Doctify team is driven by a strong belief that technology-led innovation can bring greater transparency and access to healthcare. Doctify is a healthtech platform building a revolutionary backbone for healthcare providers, doctors, and patients. Need a GP, dermatologist, dentist or cardiologist? Doctify enables users to book an appointment with a private doctor at a time that suits them. The platform makes it possible to search, compare, and book the right health specialist in less than 60 seconds.
tagline: Doctify is a healthtech platform providing SaaS tools and booking services that connect patients with private healthcare providers, making access to care faster, simpler, and more transparent.

description: Descomplica pioneered the video-first education model in Brazil and has become the leading digitally-native consumer education brand in Latin America’s largest country. At the time of Amadeus’ initial investment, the company was transforming the test-prep market by offering a fully digital, subscription-based alternative for students preparing for ENEM—Brazil’s largest university entrance exam—at a fraction of the cost of traditional tutoring. Since then, Descomplica has evolved into an accredited university, offering fully online undergraduate and postgraduate degrees across a broad range of disciplines. In 2022, it launched a B2B division focused on student employability and corporate talent acquisition. Today, millions of Brazilian students visit the Descomplica platform each month, and the company serves hundreds of thousands of paying users as it continues to reshape education in Brazil.
tagline: Descomplica is Brazil’s leading digital education platform, offering fully online degrees and career-focused learning to millions through its innovative, video-first model.

description: Creditas is a financial services platform that provides loans, insurance, and investment solutions leveraging home equity, auto equity, and payroll. With 12 years of experience, it is the largest online lending platform in Latin America and has secured investments from international funds, raising over BRL 4 billion (USD 879 million) in equity and managing a current portfolio of BRL 6 billion. Through its proprietary technology, Creditas offers products such as secured loans using vehicles or real estate as collateral, payroll loans, corporate benefits, and insurance solutions. The company has surpassed 13 million credit applications, reached a valuation of USD 4.8 billion, and executed more than 60 capital market issuances, including FIDCs, CRIs, and FIIs.
tagline: Creditas is a Latin American fintech platform using proprietary technology to deliver secured loans, insurance, and investment products at scale.

description: ContactEngine is a Conversational AI technology that enables brands to proactively engage customers in conversations that fulfil business objectives. ContactEngine automates outbound customer engagement across all channels and generates unique insights into the changing patterns of communication by applying demographic and intent analysis, linguistics and ground-breaking artificial intelligence principles to mass volumes of raw data. In 2021 ContactEngine was acquired by NICE Systems, an Israeli software enterprise company.
tagline: ContactEngine was a Conversational AI company that used advanced linguistics and intent analysis to automate and optimise customer engagement across digital channels. It was acquired by Nice Systems in 2021.

description: FiveAI was a UK-based autonomous vehicle technology company focused on developing self-driving software for urban shared transport systems. Founded with the vision of making city transport safer, more efficient, and more sustainable, FiveAI brought together top talent in artificial intelligence, engineering, and mobility to tackle the complexities of urban autonomy. The company specialized in creating the “software brain” for autonomous vehicles—sophisticated systems capable of understanding and predicting the behavior of other road users to enable safe, human-like driving. Its technology was designed to operate reliably in complex and dynamic city environments, laying the groundwork for fully autonomous shared mobility services across Europe.
tagline: FiveAI was an autonomous vehicle software company developing AI-driven systems for safe, self-driving urban transport across Europe. It was acquired by Bosch in 2022.

description: Safe Intelligence is building the foundation for truly safe AI. An Imperial College London spin-out, the company delivers deep, scalable validation of machine learning models—addressing the fragility that leads to costly pre-deployment failures and operational risk. Even advanced models can be rendered unusable due to safety concerns, but Safe Intelligence applies novel algorithmic techniques, formal verification, and robustification to restore confidence in AI systems. Its patent-pending technology powers model libraries and validation solutions across a range of domains, including finance, aviation, mobility, and robotics—helping organisations deploy machine learning safely and reliably at scale.
tagline: Safe Intelligence is a deep tech spin-out from Imperial College London developing scalable AI validation tools to ensure the safe and reliable deployment of machine learning models.

description: Refute is a technology company combating disinformation by detecting and responding to narrative-based attacks at the speed of the adversary. Using a quantitative approach, the platform fuses, traces, and scores narratives and behaviours across interconnected data to uncover and counter disinformation campaigns. These attacks are rising rapidly—driven by geopolitical instability and the accessibility of generative AI—leaving organisations increasingly vulnerable. Disinformation can inflict significant reputational and financial harm on businesses, while also eroding public trust and undermining progress on global challenges such as health, climate change, economic stability, and crime. Co-founded by Tom Garnett (CEO) and Vlad Galu (CTO), Refute brings together over 40 years of experience building world-leading data analysis systems to counter threats including terrorism, cyberattacks, identity theft, and money laundering.
tagline: Refute is a threat intelligence platform using data-driven methods to detect and disrupt disinformation campaigns targeting businesses, institutions, and society at large.

description: Sitehop is a UK-based cybersecurity company engineering the future of encryption for the quantum era. Built for speed, scalability, and sustainability, Sitehop delivers FPGA-powered, quantum-ready solutions that protect critical network data with sub-microsecond latency—10,000x faster and 10x more energy-efficient than software-based alternatives. As AI and quantum computing reshape the threat landscape, Sitehop’s hardware-first approach eliminates the trade-offs between security and performance. Its next-generation SAFE Series provides crypto-agile, high-throughput encryption and decryption for global, multi-tenant networks—securing data in motion across telecom, finance, government, and critical infrastructure. Whether securing 5G networks, cloud environments, or global transactions, Sitehop ensures that data is protected instantly, invisibly, and indestructibly—enabling organisations to operate at the speed of business without compromise.
tagline: Sitehop is a UK-based cybersecurity company delivering FPGA-powered, quantum-ready encryption with sub-microsecond latency and ultra-low power consumption to protect data in motion across global networks.

description: Vancouver-based Photonic is making one of the world’s first scalable, fault-tolerant, networked quantum computers a reality through its unique silicon spin–photon interface. The company’s technology is rooted in research led by Co-Founder and Chief Quantum Officer Dr. Stefanie Simmons and Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer Dr. Paul Terry. It combines the memory and computing advantages of spins with the connectivity and scalability of photonics. Photonic employs over 100 people and operates from its headquarters in Canada, with additional offices in the UK and US.
tagline: Photonic is building a scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computer using a unique silicon spin–photon architecture that combines quantum memory with photonic connectivity.

description: planqc is a Munich-based quantum-computing company—the first spin-out from the Munich Quantum Valley initiative—building scalable neutral-atom processors that store quantum information in individually trapped strontium atoms. Founded by scientists from the Max-Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität, the team arranges thousands of identical atoms in two- and three-dimensional optical lattices and manipulates them with ultra-stable laser pulses. This architecture offers long coherence, flexible connectivity and the fastest path to systems with thousands of qubits—an essential milestone for industry-relevant quantum advantage. Backed by the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund, planqc is delivering turnkey quantum computers and cloud access for scientific, industrial and governmental users. Current projects include a German-government programme to build a 1,000-qubit machine for the Leibniz Supercomputing Centre, and collaborative work that recently demonstrated a 1,200-atom quantum register operating continuously for more than an hour—proof of the platform’s scalability and stability.
tagline: planqc is scaling neutral-atom quantum computers built from strontium qubits—supported by the Amadeus APEX Technology Fund—to reach thousands of error-corrected qubits and unlock practical quantum advantage.

description: Based in Cambridge, UK, RoboK is a computer vision start-up on a mission to make industrial workplaces safer and more efficient using AI. A spin-out from the University of Cambridge, the company develops innovative, privacy-preserving, and cost-effective technology that maximises the value of existing industrial CCTV infrastructure. Its AI-powered platform transforms visual data into actionable insights—helping operators monitor safety risks, improve productivity, and optimise throughput. RoboK is already working with major critical infrastructure operators, including ports, to deliver real-time intelligence that enhances performance and operational oversight.
tagline: RoboK is a Cambridge-based computer vision start-up using AI to turn industrial CCTV data into actionable insights for safer, high-performing workplaces.

description: SandboxAQ is a B2B software company developing AI and quantum technologies to tackle some of the world’s most complex challenges. Its Large Quantitative Models (LQMs) drive critical advances across life sciences, financial services, navigation, cybersecurity, and more. As the world enters the third quantum revolution, SandboxAQ’s vision is to transform how businesses compete—combining AI with quantum technology to unlock new possibilities in science and industry. Amadeus became an investor in SandboxAQ following its acquisition of Cryptosense in 2022.
tagline: SandboxAQ is an enterprise software company combining AI and quantum technologies to solve major challenges across healthcare, finance, cybersecurity, and navigation.

description: Unlikely AI is a London-based technology company pioneering a new approach to artificial intelligence—delivering the full potential of modern AI while ensuring reliability, accuracy, and transparency. The company is developing products that achieve tasks previously considered impossible for computers, with a strong focus on trustworthiness and real-world usability. Founded by William Tunstall-Pedoe, Unlikely AI builds on his earlier success with Evi Technologies (formerly True Knowledge), a natural language understanding start-up acquired by Amazon in 2013. The technology became a core part of what is now Amazon Alexa.
tagline: Unlikely AI is a London-based company pioneering neurosymbolic AI that combines the power of machine learning with the reliability of symbolic computing to deliver trustworthy, explainable, next-generation AI systems.

description: Constructive Bio is expanding what biology can make. Its technology rewrites the genetic code so cells can incorporate new-to-nature chemical building blocks, giving partners a way to design proteins with properties that natural biology and conventional synthesis cannot reliably deliver. At the centre of this work is BioForge, Constructive Bio’s programmable cellular manufacturing platform. BioForge turns advanced molecular designs into manufacturable products, including complex peptides, site-specific conjugates, covalent biologics, and oral therapeutics. By connecting molecular design to scalable biological production, Constructive Bio helps its partners move from asking “can we make this?” to “what should we make next?” Through exclusive access to breakthrough science from the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology, based on research carried out by founder Professor Jason Chin, Constructive Bio alone has the ability to rewrite entire genomes and incorporate multiple non-canonical amino acids in a single molecule.
tagline: Constructive Bio designs and manufactures proteins with chemistries that do not exist in nature.

description: iPronics is a trailblazer in software-defined photonics, on a mission to make the computational power of photonics commercially accessible. Based in Spain, the company has developed the world’s first programmable optical switch, capable of supporting diverse switching strategies and processing tasks—unlocking a new era of ultra-fast, energy-efficient communication for AI clusters and data centres. At the core of its innovation is a programmable optical networking engine that dramatically improves performance while reducing power consumption, cost, and latency. This breakthrough enables seamless, scalable communication between high-performance computing systems, offering a future-proof foundation for modern data centre infrastructure. Through advanced photonic integration, iPronics increases switch complexity without increasing chip size—pushing the boundaries of optical hardware design. With its pioneering technology, iPronics is reshaping how data centres operate and accelerating the optical transformation of next-generation AI and cloud computing infrastructure.
tagline: iPronics is a Spanish deep tech company pioneering software-defined photonics with the world’s first programmable optical switch, enabling scalable, low-power communication for AI and data centre infrastructure.

description: Tenzo is an analytics and sales forecasting platform, powered by machine learning and built specifically for the restaurant industry. By integrating with POS, labour, and inventory systems, Tenzo gives operators a single, real-time view of their data—accessible via web and mobile—enabling faster, smarter decision-making on the go. The company was co-founded by CEO Christian Mouysset and CTO Adam Taylor, who first met while studying computer science. Adam went on to apply his skills in the gaming industry—working on titles such as Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater and Final Fantasy—before joining McKinsey’s big data team. Christian, meanwhile, co-founded the restaurant chain Hummus Bros, growing it to six locations. Frustrated by the lack of accessible, actionable data in hospitality, he recognised a need for change. That lightbulb moment led to the founding of Tenzo—a platform built by restaurateurs, for restaurateurs. Today, Tenzo helps restaurant teams gain complete visibility over their operations and unlock meaningful performance improvements through data.
tagline: Tenzo is a machine learning-powered analytics and forecasting platform that helps restaurants unify their data and make faster, smarter operational decisions in real time.

description: Epoch Biodesign supercharges billions of years of evolution to address humanity’s waste crisis. The company combines AI, robotic automation, and advanced synthetic biology to engineer enzymes that efficiently transform waste plastics into valuable chemicals. While the world drowns in plastic, Epoch is building the foundation of a waste-free future. Founded in 2019 by Jacob Nathan—whose inspiration began with a high school science project exploring how microbes could break down plastic—the company has grown under his leadership to a team of 32 scientists and engineers based in London. Epoch Biodesign develops natural solutions for unnatural problems, with a mission to scale and industrialise biology for a healthy planet. It has developed the first enzymes capable of transforming the hardest-to-recycle plastics into everyday chemicals. The company’s solution reduces dependence on fossil resources and lowers the carbon emissions of chemical production, all while cleaning up plastic waste.
tagline: Epoch Biodesign is a synthetic biology company that has developed enzymes to convert unrecyclable plastic waste into valuable, low-carbon chemicals using AI and advanced automation.

description: Nuclera are on a mission to better human health by increasing accessibility to proteins. Nuclera’s eProtein Discovery™ system offers rapid access to high-quality, soluble, active proteins at the benchtop, allowing scientists to automate construct screening, inform off-platform protein scale-up and deliver reliable protein in-hand (µg-mg amounts) in less than 48 hours. Nuclera’s technology integrates cell-free protein synthesis and digital microfluidics on smart cartridges, facilitating rapid development on protein projects via an automated, high-throughput protein access system. Founded in 2013 by PhD students at the University of Cambridge, the company now has a presence in Cambridge, UK and Boston, MA employing over 100 employees.
tagline: Nuclera is a biotech company making proteins more accessible through its benchtop eProtein Discovery™ system, combining cell-free synthesis and digital microfluidics for rapid, automated protein production.

description: Charco Neurotech is a Cambridge-based medical-technology spin-out from Imperial College London, developing non-invasive neuromodulation therapies for people with Parkinson’s. Its flagship wearable, CUE1 / CUE1+, sits discreetly on the sternum and delivers pulsed cueing and high-frequency vibrotactile stimulation to the peripheral nerves, easing motor symptoms such as slowness, stiffness, rigidity and freezing of gait. In pilot testing, users improved their MDS-UPDRS motor scores by an average of 7.8 points—clinically significant relief that more than 3,000 people now experience every day. The companion app lets users customise stimulation, set medication reminders and track symptoms, turning CUE1 into a personalised, data-rich therapy. Charco Neurotech Founded in 2019, the multi-award-winning team of designers, engineers and clinicians is driven by a single mission: to improve quality of life for the 10 million people living with Parkinson’s worldwide.
tagline: Charco Neurotech’s CUE1 wearable delivers individualised vibrotactile neuromodulation that helps thousands of people with Parkinson’s move more freely and live better, without surgery or drugs.

description: Cryptosense was the global leader in cryptography management software. Its platform combined automated analysis across infrastructure and applications to provide powerful insight into how cryptography is protecting sensitive data. Used by leading financial institutions and technology companies worldwide, the software delivered visibility on cryptography use, ensured encryption of critical data, and enabled innovation. The company was acquired by SandboxAQ in 2022.
tagline: Cryptosense provided cryptography management software that gave enterprises deep visibility into encryption practices, helping secure critical data across applications and infrastructure. The company was acquired by SandboxAQ in 2022.
